text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the July 25 edition of some Russian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Boris Yeltsin's decree which allows private banks to export gold bars should bring three trillion roubles to the federal budget.
- The Sukhoi company is to demonstrate its new SU-30MKI aircraft designed especially for India.
- Circulation of false promissory notes on the Russian securities market is an alarming symptom of its instability, an expert says.
- Regional governors are assigned by the government to audit local monopolies.
- A new Moscow elite club for New Russians turned out to be just another financial pyramid.
- Human rights and freedoms are priorities, says the president's press service in its comment on Boris Yeltsin's decision to turn down a controversial bill on freedom of conscience.
- The official paper publishes the president's decree on import, export and domestic market of diamonds.
- The local mafia is building up a criminal state in Kazan, an industrial city on the Volga river.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin praised the government for the country's economic achievements in the first half year of 1997.
